thread:
devon: Noticing a repeat issue during onboarding: the sample-app creates duplicate orgs when we hit 429 bursts. Looks specific to the JS SDK.
lara: Hmm, do you have a minimal repro or logs?
devon: Yep, ran locally with netem to add latency on the auth endpoint. Logs show token refresh happens and then the SDK retries the request but the Idempotency-Key header is missing. Server ends up creating the resource twice.
```
[2026-03-21T16:10:01Z] INFO http: POST /v1/orgs -> 201
[2026-03-21T16:10:01Z] WARN http: POST /v1/orgs -> 429 (rate)
[2026-03-21T16:10:01Z] INFO auth: refresh token start
[2026-03-21T16:10:02Z] INFO auth: refresh token done
[2026-03-21T16:10:02Z] INFO retry: replay POST /v1/orgs -> 201 (new row)
```
lara: Can you paste the request headers for the original vs replay?
devon: Original had `Idempotency-Key: org-flow-<uuid>` set by middleware. Replay headers are just content-type/authorization but no idempotency key.
hiro: Is this happening in python/go?
devon: Checked earlier: python and go preserve headers on retry. This looks like a JS-specific behavior where the retry path reconstructs a fresh request without copying stored outgoing headers when auth middleware causes a mid-flight refresh.
sam: Two parts to fix: preserve outgoing headers for retries and improve backoff to avoid synchronized retries. For backoff we should switch to full jitter per aws/exp guidelines. Pseudo:```
function jitterBackoff(attempt) {
  const cap = 16000;
  const base = Math.min(1000 * Math.pow(2, attempt), cap);
  return Math.floor(Math.random() * base);
}
```
devon: Also propose storing a small `_meta` object on the request like `_meta.outgoingHeaders` so downstream auth middleware and retry logic share the same canonical headers. Patch sketch:```
// outgoing middleware
req._meta = req._meta || {};
req._meta.outgoingHeaders = {...req.headers, 'Idempotency-Key': req.headers['Idempotency-Key'] || uuid()};
// retry builder
const retryReq = makeRequest({body: req.body, headers: req._meta.outgoingHeaders});
```
hiro: Add `maxRetryAfter` client config and respect `Retry-After` if server tells us to wait longer than backoff. Also allow operator opt-out to preserve current behavior for customers with custom middlewares.
lara: Tests: unit that simulates auth refresh mid-request and asserts header is present on retried envelope; e2e where sample-app run with 50 concurrent new-user flows and assert exactly 1 org per flow.
sam: CI note: there's a flaky `sdk-js::onboarding-duplicates` failing on main. Might be related. CI run: https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/24001
devon: Repro netem commands I used locally:```
# delay auth endpoint to force mid-flight refresh
sudo tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 200ms 50ms distribution normal
# later remove
sudo tc qdisc del dev lo root netem
```
lara: Thanks. Could we also make the sample-app set an explicit idempotency key per resource create as an extra safety belt? That way older SDKs or custom middlewares won't cause duplicates during onboarding.
hiro: Agreed. Also let's flip default retry strategy to include full jitter but keep it configurable via `clientOptions.retry: {strategy: 'full-jitter'}`.
sam: I'll open a PR to change the backoff and add header-stash + tests for JS SDK. Please include migration note for customers with custom retry handlers.
devon: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/497 (WIP) - includes unit tests and an e2e test job that runs the sample-app flow under netem.
ci-bot: Reminder: to be green, tests must pass under `CI=true` and `NODE_ENV=test`. Also tag flakiness if seen.
lara: After the patch, coordinate a quick Dedicated smoke test to ensure Dedicated routing/cache doesn't alter behavior.
devon: Will coordinate with eng-sre. Plan: merge patch if CI is green, cut patch release, update onboarding sample-app to set explicit idempotency keys by default.
sam: Nice. One more follow-up: add a short devex doc in onboarding README with the netem steps and guidance on how to interpret duplicate creates vs actual server bugs so new hires stop panicking.
devon: Added TODO in PR. Thanks team.
